sections.content: Hungarian is a negative-concord language: soha (never) needs nem too. Soha nem dolgozom vasárnap literally reads 'never not I-work Sunday', but it simply means 'I never work on Sunday' — dropping the nem would sound wrong, not extra polite.

items.english: I rarely work on the weekend.

sections.content: Unlike English, where 'never' and 'not' can't be stacked (you can't say 'I never don't work'), Hungarian requires exactly this stacking: soha always travels together with nem.
